title: C++ Foundations: Lifetime, Ownership, and References
description: Learn core C++ semantics through theory, compiler-backed exercises, runtime traces, and memory visualizations.

lessons.title: Update Warehouse Stock Without Creating Stale Copies
theory: Passing by value creates an independent parameter object.
A non-const lvalue reference parameter can update caller-owned state.
A const lvalue reference can inspect an existing object without copying or allowing writes through that parameter.
objectives: Diagnose a bug caused by pass-by-value.
Choose a writable reference parameter for caller-owned state.
Use a const reference for read-only access to an existing std::string.
Visualize the difference between a parameter copy and an alias.

lessons.title: Transfer Upload Payload Ownership Without Duplicating Memory
theory: Move construction transfers ownership/state from an object that is about to give up its resources.
A true ownership transfer should preserve the original resource identity instead of allocating a replacement.
Moved-from objects must remain valid, and noexcept move construction is important for standard-library container behavior.
objectives: Diagnose a move constructor that secretly duplicates an allocation.
Transfer exclusive ownership without making a second payload.
Leave the moved-from UploadPacket valid and empty.
Verify both noexcept syntax and runtime resource identity.

lessons.title: Release Video Scratch Memory Before Upload
theory: Automatic objects release their resources when their lexical scope ends.
Temporary resources should usually live in the narrowest scope that needs them.
Objects in one scope are destroyed in reverse construction order.
objectives: Recognize temporary resources whose lifetime is unnecessarily long.
Use a nested block to release scratch buffers before later work.
Observe hidden constructor/destructor instrumentation without adding tracing code to the solution.

lessons.title: unique_ptr Ownership Transfer
theory: Copying a unique_ptr is disabled because two unique owners would violate the ownership model.
std::move enables ownership to be transferred to another unique_ptr.
objectives: Use std::move to transfer a unique_ptr.
Visualize the source becoming empty after transfer.

lessons.title: Virtual Destructors
theory: Deleting a derived object through a base pointer requires a virtual base destructor for correct polymorphic destruction.
A class can have other virtual functions while still having a non-virtual destructor.
objectives: Recognize when a base destructor should be virtual.
Verify the destructor semantically with Clang AST.
